A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete 43-page 3DTrajMaster paper, including Appendices A–F. Pages 2–43 have identical extracted text and rendered pixels. First-page differences concern author information and the arXiv stamp; the scientific content supports reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original trajectory-control comparisons and ablations in Tables 2–3, additional experiments in Tables R8–R11, and user-preference results in Table R12.

after.justification: v3 retains the original experimental results in Tables 2–3 and R8–R12, together with the qualitative results throughout the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4, Algorithm 1, and Appendix A retain identical model architecture, entity-trajectory conditioning, object injector, domain adaptor, training objectives, and annealed sampling procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 360°-Motion training dataset and evaluation coverage of novel trajectories, entities, and locations. The additional dataset analyses and qualitative scenarios in Appendices E–F are also identical.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains Base T2V, MotionCtrl, Tora, and Direct-a-Video. The comparator subsets displayed in Figure 6 and the user-preference comparison in Table R12 are unchanged.

E3.justification: Training budgets, model size, preprocessing, the 100 evaluation pairs, human-pose evaluation procedure, and video-quality metrics are identical. Appendix ablation protocols and the 53-sample user survey are also unchanged.

E4.justification: Both retain the same component ablations in Table 3, hyperparameter and negative-pose analyses in Tables R8–R11, entity-distribution analysis in Figure S10, and editing/generalization examples in Figures S11–S31.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The point-estimate and user-preference reporting practices remain identical.

E6.justification: All numerical tables and qualitative results are unchanged. For example, Table 2 reports the same all-entity errors of 0.398 m and 0.277 degrees for 3DTrajMaster in both versions; Tables R8–R12 also match exactly.

T1.justification: The task formulation, diffusion objectives, and attention/adaptor equations (1)–(4) are identical. No mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added, removed, or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction’s contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about multi-entity 6DoF control, the dataset, generalization, and state-of-the-art trajectory accuracy.

C2.justification: Interpretations of motion fusion and video-quality/pose-accuracy tradeoffs are identical. Section 5 and Appendix D retain the same limitations concerning animal editing, local motions and interactions, and generation of at most three entities.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hardware, hyperparameters, preprocessing instructions, backbone description, and evaluation prompts remain unchanged. The project-page link and technical access information are also retained.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix B, and the bibliography are identical. The positioning relative to earlier 2D motion-control and 3D-aware video-generation methods is unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 removes the dagger beside Xiao Fu and the footnote stating that the work was done during an internship at KwaiVGI, Kuaishou Technology. Scientific prose, terminology, and section organization remain identical.

P2.justification: The first page has small author-line spacing and footnote layout adjustments, plus an updated arXiv version/date stamp. All figures, tables, captions, and the layouts of pages 2–43 are identical.

improvement.justification: v3 only changes first-page author information and the arXiv stamp. The method, experimental evidence, explanations, reproducibility information, and all appendices remain identical, so these administrative edits do not materially improve or diminish the paper’s overall quality.
